## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A short single-juan *xíngzhuàng* 行狀 ("conduct record" — the formal Confucian funerary genre listing the principal events of a deceased subject's life as a basis for an official biography) of the great Táng pilgrim and translator [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98) (Xuánzàng, 602–664), composed shortly after his death in 664 by the monk [冥詳](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%86%A5%E8%A9%B3) (Míngxiáng). Preserved in the Taishō (T50 no. 2052). The work is the earliest extant biographical document on Xuánzàng, predating both the *Dà cí'ēnsì sānzàng fǎshī zhuàn* of [慧立](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E7%AB%8B) and [彥悰](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BD%A5%E6%82%B0) ([KR6r0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6r/KR6r0043)) and the entry in the *Xù gāosēng zhuàn* of [道宣](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%93%E5%AE%A3) ([KR6r0061](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6r/KR6r0061)).

**Abstract**

The *xíngzhuàng* genre is a formal funerary document listing the deceased's birthplace, ancestry, principal offices, achievements, and death — typically composed for the use of subsequent biographers. [冥詳](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%86%A5%E8%A9%B3)'s *xíngzhuàng* of [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98) supplies precisely such a record: birth in Luòzhōu 洛州 in 602, family of the Chén 陳 surname, early entry into the saṃgha, Xuánzàng's celebrated journey to India (629–645), the seventeen years of pilgrimage, the return with manuscripts and relics, the imperial reception under Tàizōng, the long Cháng'ān years of translation activity (645–664), and the death at Yùhuá-gōng 玉華宮 in 664.

The composition window is bracketed by Xuánzàng's death (664) and the production of the more elaborate *Cí'ēnsì zhuàn* of [慧立](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E7%AB%8B) / [彥悰](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BD%A5%E6%82%B0) in the 680s; a date bracket of 664–670 is the safe range, with most scholars favouring the years immediately after Xuánzàng's death. The work is short — only a few thousand characters — but it is the *direct* primary biographical source for [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98) and a foundational document for all subsequent biographies.

[冥詳](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%86%A5%E8%A9%B3) is otherwise little documented; he was clearly a disciple or younger associate of Xuánzàng's translation bureau at Dà Cí'ēnsì 大慈恩寺.
